mode: generate with identity references, then targeted padding edit
prompts: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit the attached 6-column by 2-row player attack sprite sheet for safe texture atlas packing. KEEP all 12 character identities, costumes, hand/weapon assignments, six attack poses per row, natural proportions, camera direction, frame order, colors, material details and transparent background unchanged. The ONLY change is generous uniform spacing: shrink every full character uniformly to 70 percent of its current size about its feet, and place each character with torso aligned to the center of its own equal-sized cell. Keep both rows and exactly six columns. Use a wide 3:1 transparent canvas. Every sword tip, lantern, cloak and especially every mutant claw must be entirely contained inside its own equal-width cell with at least 15 percent of cell width of EMPTY transparent padding on BOTH sides. Do not let claws overhang the next column. Keep generous empty transparent gutters across the entire image at each of the five exact column boundaries and the one exact row boundary. Top row feet lie on one common baseline at 85 percent of the top row's height; bottom row feet on the corresponding baseline at 85 percent of the bottom row's height. Constant body scale within each row. Preserve the exact visible arm-extension to recoil-to-idle progression in the original. Do not invent new poses or duplicate frames, do not add text or effects or grid lines, no ground shadows or background. Keep genuinely transparent RGBA alpha. Make the twelve figures VISIBLY SMALLER relative to the canvas than the input sheet, do not crop or auto-fit the canvas around them.
